title: Aescin can alleviate NAFLD through Keap1-Nrf2 by activating antioxidant and autophagy.
authors: Yu, Hao; Yan, Siru; Jin, Meiyu; Wei, Yunfei; Zhao, Lilei; Cheng, Jiaqi; Ding, Lu; Feng, Haihua
journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology
one_liner_zh: 研究Aescin通过Keap1-Nrf2通路缓解NAFLD，涉及蛋白-蛋白互作而非蛋白-DNA互作，仅含计算机模拟对接，无TF-DNA结合建模，与本课题关联微弱。
abstract: BACKGROUND: Non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) is a common metabolic liver disease worldwide. It has been proven that aescin (Aes), a bioactive compound derived from the ripe dried fruit of Aesculus chinensis Bunge, has a number of physiologically active properties like anti-inflammatory and anti-edema, however it has not been investigated as a potential solution for NAFLD. PURPOSE: This study's major goal was to determine whether Aes can treat NAFLD and the mechanism underlying its therapeutic benefits. METHODS: We constructed HepG2 cell models in vitro that were affected by oleic and palmitic acids, as well as in vivo models for acute lipid metabolism disorder caused by tyloxapol and chronic NAFLD caused by high-fat diet. RESULTS: We discovered that Aes could promote autophagy, activate the Nrf2 pathway, and ameliorate lipid accumulation and oxidative stress both in vitro and in vivo. Nevertheless, in Autophagy-related proteins 5 (Atg5) and Nrf2 knockout mice, Aes lost its curative impact on NAFLD. Computer simulations show that Aes might interact with Keap1, which might allow Aes to increase Nrf2 transfer into the nucleus and perform its function. Importantly, Aes's stimulation of autophagy in the liver was hampered in Nrf2 knockout mice. This suggested that the impact of Aes in inducing autophagy may be connected to the Nrf2 pathway. CONCLUSION: We first discovered Aes's regulating effects on liver autophagy and oxidative stress in NAFLD. And we found Aes may combine the Keap1 and regulate autophagy in the liver by affecting Nrf2 activation to exert its protective effect.
abstract_zh: 背景：非酒精性脂肪性肝病（NAFLD）是全球常见的代谢性肝病。已有研究证明，七叶皂苷钠（Aes），一种来源于娑罗子（Aesculus chinensis Bunge）成熟干燥果实中的生物活性化合物，具有多种生理活性特性，如抗炎和抗水肿，但其作为NAFLD潜在治疗方案的潜力尚未被研究。目的：本研究的主要目标是确定Aes是否能治疗NAFLD，并探讨其治疗益处背后的机制。方法：我们构建了体外受油酸和棕榈酸影响的HepG2细胞模型，以及由泰洛沙泊引起的急性脂质代谢紊乱和由高脂饮食引起的慢性NAFLD的体内模型。结果：我们发现Aes能促进自噬、激活Nrf2通路，并在体外和体内改善脂质积累和氧化应激。然而，在自噬相关蛋白5（Atg5）和Nrf2敲除小鼠中，Aes对NAFLD的治疗效果丧失。计算机模拟显示，Aes可能与Keap1相互作用，这可能使Aes增强Nrf2向细胞核的转移并发挥其功能。重要的是，在Nrf2敲除小鼠中，Aes对肝脏自噬的刺激受到阻碍。这表明Aes诱导自噬的作用可能与Nrf2通路相关。结论：我们首次发现Aes在NAFLD中对肝脏自噬和氧化应激的调节作用。并且我们发现Aes可能通过结合Keap1并影响Nrf2激活来调节肝脏自噬，从而发挥其保护作用。
